titel: Essential and dispensable insurance in the US
kurz: Which risks justify insurance, which four kinds of coverage protect a US household against ruin, and which policies you can do without.

bloecke.md:
Insurance is an exchange, not a savings contract. The insured person pays a small, certain amount and in return receives the promise that a large, uncertain amount will not hit their household. The price of this promise is made up of the expected loss plus loadings for administration, sales commissions and profit margin. Across the insured pool as a whole, policyholders therefore inevitably pay in more than they get out, because otherwise no insurer could survive.

This gives rise to the most important rule when choosing insurance. Losses that can be paid from the emergency fund or from two months' salary are ones you bear yourself. The reason is that the loading for administration and sales is highest in percentage terms for small losses. A protection plan for a $800 device therefore mainly offers convenience and hardly any additional security.

The question is what happens to your household if a loss occurs. The probability of the loss is not decisive for this. You do not insure a risk you can bear yourself. You insure a risk you cannot bear even if it is very unlikely.

bloecke.titel: Risks by size of loss and probability
bloecke.unter: Only the bottom-right quadrant justifies a policy. Most of the policies sold at checkout cover risks from the top-left quadrant.

felder.text: Cracked screen, glasses, small appliance repairs, a dented bumper. Happens often, costs little. In the end the premium is higher than the sum of the losses.
Need for long-term care in old age. When the loss is very likely to occur, the premium approaches the loss. Saving and planning matter at least as much as insuring here.
Flight accident cover, lost luggage, phone theft on vacation. Rare and small. Any policy for these is pure cost.
Injuring someone else, long-term disability, death of the main earner, serious illness, house fire. Rare, but they destroy livelihoods.

bloecke.md:
## Required coverage and voluntary policies

In the US, very little insurance is required by federal law. Since 2019 there has been no federal penalty for going without health insurance, although a few states, among them California, Massachusetts, New Jersey and Rhode Island, as well as the District of Columbia, have their own requirement. Auto liability insurance is required in nearly every state. Through payroll taxes, almost every employee is automatically covered by Social Security, which includes disability and survivor benefits, and by Medicare. Unemployment insurance and, in almost all states, workers' compensation are paid for by the employer. Lenders add their own requirements: a mortgage comes with mandatory homeowners insurance and, for a federally backed loan on a building in a high-risk flood zone, flood insurance. Everything else is voluntary and is therefore sold particularly hard.

Four kinds of coverage protect against the risks that can ruin a household financially: liability coverage (auto, homeowners or renters, possibly an umbrella policy), long-term disability insurance, term life insurance if someone depends on your income, and health insurance. A household that has these four and no other policies is better protected than many households with a drawer full of contracts.

## Liability coverage

If you injure someone, you are liable under state tort law for their medical bills, lost earnings and pain and suffering, and there is no upper limit. For a young victim with permanent injuries, the damages can run into millions. Whatever your insurance does not pay, you owe personally. A court judgment can be enforced through liens, bank levies and wage garnishment, which federal law caps at 25% of disposable earnings in most cases (15 U.S.C. § 1673); some states protect more.

Unlike in some countries, there is usually no standalone personal liability policy in the US. Personal liability cover is part of a homeowners or renters policy, often with limits such as $100,000 or $300,000, and auto liability is part of the car policy. State minimum limits for auto liability are often only tens of thousands of dollars per injured person, far below what a serious accident costs. Anyone with assets or a good income should therefore choose high limits and consider an **umbrella policy**. It sits on top of the auto and home policies, is typically sold in steps of $1 million and requires certain minimum limits on the underlying policies. Renters insurance includes liability cover as well and is one of the cheapest ways to get it. Check whether your policy covers your dog: some insurers exclude certain breeds or dog bites altogether.

Suppose an umbrella policy with $1 million of cover costs $300 a year. That is around $3,333 of cover for every dollar of premium. This ratio is possible because multi-million-dollar claims are rare, and for the same reason the cover is cheap. Choosing low limits on the auto policy saves only a small amount a year and in return leaves you exposed to exactly the large losses the policy is meant for. Ask for actual quotes, because premiums vary by state, driving record and the number of cars and drivers.

## Long-term disability

For anyone in work, their future earning capacity is by far their largest asset. A 30-year-old with $4,000 of monthly take-home pay will earn around $1.78 million in purely nominal terms by the age of 67 (37 years times twelve months times $4,000), without counting any raises. Nobody would leave a portfolio of this size uninsured, yet their own earning capacity often remains unprotected.

According to the Social Security Administration, a 20-year-old worker has about a one-in-four chance of becoming disabled before reaching full retirement age. Most long-term disabilities are caused by illness, such as musculoskeletal disorders, cancer, heart disease or mental illness, not by accidents. The younger you are, the more of your income is still at stake.

bloecke.titel: Future earnings at stake by age (nominal, $4,000 net a month until age 67)
bloecke.unter: Own calculation without raises or interest. Even at 55, more than half a million dollars of income is still ahead.

bloecke.md:
Public protection for this case is limited. There is no federal requirement for paid sick leave or short-term disability benefits. Only a handful of states, including California, Hawaii, New Jersey, New York and Rhode Island, run state disability insurance programs, and several states have added paid family and medical leave programs. Many employers offer short-term disability cover for the first weeks or months.

For long-term cases, Social Security Disability Insurance (SSDI) remains. It applies a strict definition. You must be unable to do any substantial gainful activity because of a medical condition that is expected to last at least twelve months or to result in death, and the Social Security Administration (SSA) considers whether you could do *any* other work in the national economy given your age, education and experience, not just your previous job. In 2026, earnings above $1,690 a month (for people who are not blind) generally count as substantial gainful activity. Benefits start only after a waiting period of five full months, Medicare coverage only after 24 months of benefits, and the benefit is based on your lifetime earnings record, not your last salary. Many initial applications are denied, and appeals can take a long time.

SSDI is no substitute for private disability insurance, because it does not protect your occupation. A surgeon who could still work at a desk is not disabled under Social Security rules.

Employer group long-term disability (LTD) insurance is valuable but often not enough. It typically replaces around 60% of base salary up to a monthly cap, frequently switches after two years from your own occupation to *any* occupation, ends when you leave the job, and its benefits are taxable if the employer paid the premiums. Accidental death and dismemberment (AD&D) and accident-only policies are no substitute either, because they do not cover illness, the most common cause. Workers' compensation pays only for work-related injuries and illnesses.

bloecke.md:
A common target is that group and individual coverage together replace around 60% of gross income. Insurers rarely allow more, because benefits from a policy you pay for yourself with after-tax money are tax-free (IRS Publication 525) and therefore already close to your take-home pay. The premium is often quoted at around 1% to 3% of annual income, depending heavily on occupation, age, health and the features chosen.

When choosing a policy, the contract language matters more than the premium. Important features are an **own-occupation** definition of disability (otherwise the insurer can point to another job you could theoretically do), a policy that is **non-cancelable and guaranteed renewable** (the insurer cannot cancel it or raise the premium as long as you pay), a [[Guaranteed insurability option|future increase option]] that lets you raise the benefit later without new health questions, a residual or partial disability benefit for a gradual return to work, a cost-of-living adjustment rider and a benefit period that runs until 65 or 67. The **elimination period**, usually 90 days, should match your emergency fund: a longer waiting period makes the policy cheaper.

Health questions must be answered completely and truthfully. If you misstate your medical history, the insurer can contest the policy, typically within the first two years, and in the case of fraud even later. This happens when a claim is made, that is, when the money is needed. Copies of your medical records from recent years help you answer correctly.

Working with an independent broker who can approach several insurers is advisable. Information from applications is shared through MIB, a database used by life and health insurers, and a decline can make later applications more difficult. Under the Fair Credit Reporting Act you can request your MIB file free of charge once a year and have errors corrected.

## Term life insurance

Term life insurance pays a fixed sum to your beneficiaries if you die during the term, typically 10, 20 or 30 years, and does not build up any cash value. It is necessary for main or sole earners with a family and for couples with a mortgage. For single people without dependants it is superfluous, because there is then nobody whose standard of living depends on the insured person's income.

A common rule of thumb in the US is ten times gross annual salary; a needs analysis is more precise. It adds up the income your family would need until the children are independent, the mortgage balance and future education costs, and subtracts existing savings and the survivor benefits that Social Security pays to young children and to a spouse caring for them. Because the benefit is standardized, comparing quotes is more worthwhile here than for almost any other policy. Group life insurance through your employer is often only one or two times salary and usually ends with the job. Suicide is typically excluded only during the first two years.

bloecke.titel: Death benefit by rule of thumb (plus the mortgage balance, minus existing savings)

bloecke.md:
## Health insurance

Most working-age people are covered through an employer plan, whose premium share is usually deducted from pay before taxes. Without employer coverage, the ACA marketplace (HealthCare.gov or a state exchange) offers individual plans; premium tax credits based on household income lower the cost, and Congress has changed how generous they are several times, so check the current rules for your plan year. People with low incomes may qualify for Medicaid, whose rules differ by state. From 65, Medicare takes over. You can enroll in or switch marketplace and employer plans during the annual open enrollment period or within a special enrollment period after events such as losing other coverage, marriage, the birth of a child or a move (usually 60 days). After leaving a job, COBRA lets you keep the employer plan for generally up to 18 months, but you then pay up to 102% of the full premium yourself.

The easiest saving in this field is choosing the plan with the lowest *total* expected cost, not the lowest premium. The deciding figures are the premium, the deductible, the coinsurance and the **out-of-pocket maximum**, which ACA-compliant plans must have for covered in-network care, plus whether your doctors are in the network. A high-deductible health plan can be paired with a health savings account (HSA). For 2026, up to $4,400 (self-only) or $8,750 (family) can be contributed; contributions through payroll are free of income tax and payroll tax, and withdrawals for qualified medical expenses are tax-free.

bloecke.titel: Comparing two plans by total cost (illustrative calculation)
bloecke.md:
Plan A costs $150 a month with a $500 deductible, 20% coinsurance and a $3,000 out-of-pocket maximum. Plan B costs $50 a month with a $3,000 deductible, 20% coinsurance and a $6,000 out-of-pocket maximum.

Without any medical bills, plan A costs $1,800 a year and plan B $600. With $5,000 of covered bills, plan A costs $3,200 ($1,800 premium, $500 deductible, 20% of $4,500) and plan B $4,000 ($600 premium, $3,000 deductible, 20% of $2,000). From around $20,000 of bills, both plans reach their out-of-pocket maximum: plan A then costs $4,800 and plan B $6,600 at most.

The cheaper premium wins in healthy years, the lower out-of-pocket maximum in bad ones. If you choose plan B, the $1,200 lower premium belongs in an HSA or the emergency fund so that the higher worst case can be paid. The comparison has to be made with your own expected usage and the actual plan documents (Summary of Benefits and Coverage).

## Dispensable and supplementary insurance

Extended warranties and protection plans, phone insurance, flight accident insurance, credit life and [[Payment protection insurance|credit disability insurance]] sold with loans, AD&D as a replacement for life insurance, cancer and other single-disease policies, and life insurance on children are of low priority or superfluous. Rental car coverage at the counter often duplicates what your auto policy or credit card already provides; check before you travel. Prepaid legal plans are a borderline case: they help with simple matters such as wills or letters, but often exclude exactly the expensive disputes.

Two policies, on the other hand, are worth considering even though they are not among the four core kinds of coverage. For homeowners and renters, this is **flood insurance**, because standard homeowners and renters policies exclude flood damage. Policies from the National Flood Insurance Program usually take effect only after a 30-day waiting period, so they cannot be bought when the storm is already forecast. In earthquake regions, the same applies to earthquake cover. The second policy is **travel medical insurance** for trips abroad, because Original Medicare generally does not pay for care outside the US and many other plans pay little or nothing there.

bloecke.titel: Annual cost of the two plans at different levels of medical bills
bloecke.unter: Illustrative calculation from the example above: premium plus deductible and coinsurance, capped at the out-of-pocket maximum. Neither plan is better in every year.

bloecke.md:
With an [[Excess (insurance)|insurance deductible]], the policyholder bears small losses themselves. This makes sense because handling a $300 claim costs the insurer almost as much as the loss itself. The premium falls accordingly.

Suppose a homeowners policy costs $1,200 a year, and raising the deductible from $500 to $1,000 lowers the premium by 10%, that is, by $120 a year. After just over four claim-free years, the extra $500 of one claim is offset by the savings, and from the fifth year onwards the saving stays with you. The calculation only becomes unfavourable with more than one claim every four years. In addition, auto and home insurers in the US often raise premiums after claims, so small claims are frequently not worth filing anyway.

## Cash-value life insurance

Whole life, universal life, indexed universal life and variable universal life combine a death benefit with a savings component, the cash value. They are hardly suitable as an investment. A large part of the premiums in the first years goes to sales commissions and costs, surrender charges often apply for ten years or more, and the guaranteed growth of the cash value is low. Indexed policies add caps and participation rates that limit how much of the market's gain reaches you.

The tax advantages are often overstated in sales. The death benefit is generally free of income tax (26 U.S.C. § 101), but that applies to term life insurance just as well. The cash value grows tax-deferred; if you surrender the policy, the amount above the premiums paid is taxed as ordinary income. A policy funded too quickly becomes a modified endowment contract (MEC), and then withdrawals and loans are taxed and, before age 59½, generally subject to an additional 10% tax. For most households, tax-advantaged retirement accounts such as a 401(k) or an IRA offer the same deferral at far lower cost. Cash-value policies have a place in special situations, for example estate planning for very large estates.

bloecke.titel: Example: buy term and invest the difference
bloecke.md:
Suppose a whole life policy costs $400 a month and a 20-year term policy with the same death benefit costs $40 a month. The difference of $360 a month adds up to $86,400 over 20 years. Invested at an assumed 5% a year, it grows to around $148,000.

The whole life policy only comes out ahead if its cash value after 20 years exceeds this amount, after surrender charges. Look at the guaranteed column of the policy illustration, not only at the projected column, which rests on assumptions about future dividends or crediting rates. The rates in this example are assumptions for the calculation; actual premiums depend on age, health and the insurer.

bloecke.md:
The criticism of new policies does not automatically apply to old ones. Older whole life policies sometimes carry guaranteed rates well above what new policies offer, and the surrender charges may already have expired. If you want out, compare the options first: a reduced paid-up policy, a loan against the cash value, or a tax-free exchange into another policy or annuity under Section 1035 of the Internal Revenue Code. A surrender can trigger income tax on the gain.

An existing disability or term life policy should never be cancelled before the replacement policy is in force. The new policy requires a new health assessment, starts a new contestability period, and the premium rises with every year of age.

schritte.titel: List existing policies and sort them by maximum loss
schritte.text: Write down all policies one below the other with annual premium, coverage amount, deductible and renewal date. Then check for each policy whether the loss could be covered from savings. Every policy for which this is true goes on the list for cancellation.
Choose high liability limits on the auto and homeowners or renters policy and get a quote for a $1 million umbrella policy if you own a home, have savings or a good income.

schritte.titel: Check and close the disability gap
schritte.text: Read the employer's LTD plan: benefit percentage, cap, definition of disability and who pays the premium. Close the gap with an individual own-occupation policy, and assess the contract terms before the premium.

schritte.titel: Term life insurance only if others depend on you financially
schritte.text: With a partner, children or a mortgage, calculate the need, buy level term insurance for the years the need lasts and compare several quotes. Otherwise, no policy is needed.

schritte.titel: Choose the health plan by total cost, add flood and travel cover where relevant
schritte.text: In open enrollment, compare premium, deductible and out-of-pocket maximum with your expected usage and check the network. Check your flood risk, and buy travel medical insurance for trips abroad.

schritte.titel: Only cancel once the replacement is in place
schritte.text: Minor policies can be cancelled immediately, core coverage only once the new policy has been issued and is in force.

mitnehmen: Only losses that would ruin the household are insured. Anything that can be paid from the emergency fund stays uninsured, because the cost loading is highest for small losses.
Liability for injuring others has no upper limit. High limits on auto and home policies plus an umbrella policy cost little compared with the risk they cover.
SSDI pays only if you cannot do any substantial work at all, and employer LTD often covers only part of base salary. An individual own-occupation policy closes the gap.
Choose health plans by total expected cost, including deductible and out-of-pocket maximum, not by the premium alone.
Risk cover and investment belong in separate contracts. Existing cash-value policies are reviewed before they are surrendered, because a reduced paid-up policy or a 1035 exchange may be better.

begriffe.text: Personal liability insurance that pays above the limits of your auto and homeowners or renters policies, typically in steps of $1 million. It requires minimum limits on the underlying policies.

Insurance that pays a monthly benefit if illness or injury prevents you from working for an extended period. It protects income, not health. Coverage can come from an employer group plan or an individual policy.

Definition of disability under which you count as disabled if you can no longer perform the material duties of your own occupation, even if you could do other work. It is the US counterpart to waiving referral to other occupations.
Waiting period between the start of a disability and the first benefit payment, often 90 days. A longer elimination period lowers the premium and should match the emergency fund.
The most you pay in a plan year for covered in-network care through deductibles, coinsurance and copays. After that, the plan pays 100% of covered costs. Premiums do not count toward it.
Tax-free exchange of a life insurance policy or annuity for another under Section 1035 of the Internal Revenue Code. It avoids the income tax that a surrender would trigger on the gain.
